BUG REPORT (verbatim from user):
"I turned on `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` in my app so that malformed dates blow up loudly instead of silently producing invalid values, and I parse intervals with `Interval.fromISO`. When I pass an interval that combines a date with a duration, it throws instead of returning the interval:

```js
Settings.throwOnInvalid = true;
Interval.fromISO("2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M");
```

I expected a valid interval back, the same one I get when `throwOnInvalid` is left at its default, but instead I get `InvalidArgumentError: Invalid DateTime`. The same thing happens with the duration first (`"PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00"`), even though both halves of the string are valid and parse fine on their own."

Your job: find the root cause in /luxon/src (start with src/interval.js `fromISO`, and how DateTime/Duration parsing interacts with Settings.throwOnInvalid in src/settings.js and src/datetime.js), fix it minimally so that Interval.fromISO with a date+duration combination returns the correct valid Interval when Settings.throwOnInvalid is true (and behaves identically to the default-throwOnInvalid case), and verify with a small node/babel-node script plus the existing jest test suites for interval, datetime and duration.

IMPORTANT: before changing anything, run the relevant existing test files (e.g. `cd /luxon && npx jest test/interval test/datetime test/duration`) and record which tests already fail (baseline). "I was adding 61 days to 0099-12-31 and expected to land on 0100-03-02, but the result was 0100-03-01. This happens when the addition crosses the year 100 boundary and goes through February.

```js
const d = DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 });
d.toISODate(); // "0100-03-01", but I expected "0100-03-02"
```"

## Bug #2.3 — FixedOffsetZone accepts non-numeric offsets

### Root cause
`src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` stored the constructor argument verbatim (`this.fixed = offset`) and its `isValid` getter was hard-coded to `return true`. So `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT")` reported a valid zone. `DateTime`'s zone validation is correct and already works off `zone.isValid` (`src/datetime.js:385` in the constructor, plus `fromMillis`/`fromObject`/`setZone` paths), so once the zone reports itself invalid, DateTime correctly produces `unsupported zone`. No change was needed in `datetime.js` or `zoneUtil.js`.

### Change (only source file touched)
`src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` — 2 lines:
```diff
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
-import { formatOffset, signedOffset } from "../impl/util.js";
+import { formatOffset, signedOffset, isNumber } from "../impl/util.js";
@@ -89,6 +89,6 @@ export default class FixedOffsetZone extends Zone {
   /** @override **/
   get isValid() {
-    return true;
+    return isNumber(this.fixed);
   }
```
(`git diff --stat`: 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-). No test file touched; `git status --short test/` is empty. The pre-existing modifications to `src/datetime.js`, `src/impl/util.js`, `src/interval.js` are from other bug fixes in this container, not mine.)

### Reported example (before → after)
Before: `zone.isValid` → `true`; `dt.isValid, dt.invalidReason` → `true undefined`.
After (`npx babel-node /tmp/reported.js`):
```
false
false 'unsupported zone'
```

- Baseline (`cd /luxon && npx jest test/zones test/datetime test/info`): `Tests: 2 failed, 638 passed, 640 total` — the 2 known pre-existing French-locale/ICU failures in `test/datetime/toFormat.test.js` (`FFF`/`FFFF`, expected `09:23:54` vs received `9:23:54`).
